results.title: From Obligation to Specification: A Survey on Validating EU AI Act Requirements in RE
results.snippet: With the EU AI Act entering into force, organizations developing or operating AI systems face new obligations on transparency, risk management, and traceability. For Requirements Engineering (RE), these obligations must be translated into testable, auditable requirements and verifiable evidence. However, many organizations currently lack systematic processes to achieve this. We hypothesize that LLM-based agentic validation tools can support this translation, thereby helping to close this gap. We present a mixed-method exploratory study with expert interviews (N=10) and an online survey (N=15)…

results.title: Are LLM Assistants Regulatory Ready? Answers from regenold's 2026 EU AI Act Q&A Challenge
results.snippet: Large language model (LLM) assistants are increasingly proposed for regulatory affairs, yet their reliability in regulatory tasks remains unclear. We introduce the EU AI Act Q&A Benchmark, an expert-curated benchmark of 110 open-ended questions about the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). Each question comes with an exemplary answer, question-specific correctness criteria, and expected references. Evaluation measures answer correctness, reference quality, conciseness, tone, and latency, with a multi-turn ``hard mode'' testing responses to simulated user pushback. We also present the resul…

results.title: An Empirical Study and Assessment of EU AI Act Compliance Checkers
results.snippet: The EU AI Act introduces extensive compliance requirements for organizations that develop, deploy, or integrate AI systems. Many of these requirements are directly relevant to security and privacy, while also addressing closely related issues such as data governance, transparency, accuracy, and robustness. However, stakeholders such as small-to-medium businesses and individual developers often lack the legal expertise required to interpret these obligations and translate them into engineering and governance practices. This disconnect creates challenges for implementing the EU AI Act and may l…

results.title: Making AI Compliance Evidence Machine-Readable
results.snippet: AI Assurance -- producing the machine-readable evidence required to demonstrate compliance with AI governance frameworks -- has mature policy scaffolding but lacks the infrastructure to operationalize it. Organizations building high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act face a gap: frameworks such as the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, and NIST AI RMF specify what to assure but provide no executable format for how. findings.point: OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language) 被提议作为 AI 治理的机器可读合规证据交换格式，配合 16 个属性扩展覆盖生命周期阶段、执行语义、风险追溯与风险接受辩护，形成三层 Compliance-as-Code 架构（策略、证据、执行）
findings.evidence: 论文提出将 NIST OSCAL 标准（原用于 FedRAMP 网络安全合规）迁移至 AI 治理，定义 16 个属性扩展，构建 policy/evidence/enforcement 三层架构，生成机器可读的保证证据
findings.attention: 中等：2026-04 最新预印本，针对 EU AI Act/ISO 42001/NIST AI RMF 合规落地痛点，但为预印本且无引用/星标数据
findings.recommendation: ★★★☆☆：直接切中合规工具链标准化需求，架构设计完整，但为预印本且缺乏开源实现与第三方验证

results.title: Faith in AI can narrow the futures individuals consider
results.snippet: Artificial intelligence (AI) predictions are increasingly used to inform human decisions. Here, using a behavioral implementation of the classic Newcomb's paradox in 1,305 participants, we show that AI predictions can also shape the reasoning people use to make a decision. In this paradigm, perceived predictive authority can alter how people reason about their future actions, leading them to forgo a guaranteed reward. Over 40% of participants treated AI as such a predictive authority about their own behavior, significantly increasing the odds of forgoing the guaranteed reward by a factor of 3…

findings.point: AI 研究的可复现性危机正在削弱政策制定者的治理能力，缺乏严格的复现协议导致信噪比低、监管俘获风险高
findings.evidence: 论文指出当前 AI 发布速度快但缺乏强科学标准，弱复现协议侵蚀政策制定权力，建议采用更严格的复现指南以助治理
findings.authority: arXiv 预印本 (cs.AI)，未经同行评审
findings.attention: 中：直接切中 AI 治理的评测科学性瓶颈，被引用为治理前沿议题
findings.recommendation: ★★★★☆：权威性中等但主题高度契合‘评测科学性不足’核心瓶颈，值得作为治理基础设施切入点研读

findings.point: AI 事件治理缺乏统一定义、分类体系、监测实践、报告机制与事后分析框架，属典型‘标准滞后、执行碎片化’领域
findings.evidence: 论文系统梳理现有事件治理框架，指出定义/分类/监测/报告/分析五大环节均存在空白，呼吁建立完善的事件治理基础设施
findings.authority: arXiv 预印本 (cs.CY)，未经同行评审
findings.attention: 中：聚焦事件治理全链路，对应‘技术标准滞后’与‘跨境执法碎片化’痛点
findings.recommendation: ★★★★☆：直接列举开放问题清单，适合作为审计/合规 SaaS 产品需求挖掘的源头参考

findings.point: 提出五层治理框架（监管原则→标准→合规评估→认证→执行），旨在弥合高层法规与落地合规机制的断层
findings.evidence: 框架显式连接 regulation、standards、conformity assessment、certification、enforcement 五层，解决‘法规难落地、标准缺失、认证缺位’的结构性缺口
findings.authority: arXiv 预印本 (cs.CY)，未经同行评审
findings.attention: 中高：提供结构化落地路径，对应‘合规 SaaS、审计员认证体系’蓝海机会的理论支撑
findings.recommendation: ★★★★★：框架可直接映射为产品模块（合规评估引擎、认证工作流），落地价值最高

findings.point: 人类对 AI 预测权威的过度信任会窄化决策空间、降低收益，揭示‘人机信任校准’是治理不可忽视的行为层面瓶颈
findings.evidence: 1305 人实验显示 40%+ 参与者将 AI 视为预测权威，放弃确定奖励概率升 3.39 倍，收益降 10.7-42.9%，即使预测反复失效效应仍存
findings.authority: arXiv 预印本 (cs.HC)，未经同行评审
findings.attention: 中：行为实证强，但距‘治理落地’尚有一层转化距离
findings.recommendation: ★★★☆☆：为‘保险定价/审计指标中的人因风险参数’提供实证基础，属辅助性证据
